_comment: Types round 8 (docs/notes/types_8.md): Lua 3.1's objects in LUA.DLL, as Grim's build lays them out (checked against the code: luaF_newproto / newclosure, newone / insert, luaH_new / get / set, the GC's mark and free functions). Every collectable object starts with Lua's GCnode {next, marked}; here as pNext / nMarked of each structure. A TObject's value is a union (number, string, table, ...): as dwValue, the bits, since ghidra_types.h holds structures only.

structs.name: TObject
structs.comment: A Lua value: its type tag (Grim's numbering, build/overrides.c: -1 number, -2 string, -3 table, -4 Lua function, -5 C function, -6 task, -7 nil, -8 userdata, 0 and up user tags) and the value.
fields: the value: a float for a number, else a pointer (TaggedString *, Hash *, TProtoFunc *, Closure *) or a C function

structs.name: TaggedString
structs.comment: A string or a userdata of the string table (lstring.c). Grim's order: constindex before the hash (Lua 3.1 has them the other way).
fields: GCnode: the next of its list (itself when new)
0 for a string, -1 for a userdata
the hash the string table files it under
a string: the global of that name (nil when undefined); a userdata: its tag (nTtype) and pointer (dwValue)
the characters of a string, NUL-terminated, as long as the string

structs.name: StringTable
structs.comment: One of the hashed string tables (lstring.c stringtable; the state's string_root holds 61).
fields: strings in it (grow() doubles the slots at 2 / 3 full)

structs.name: Node
structs.comment: One slot of a table's hash part (ltable.c): key and value; a nil key is an empty slot.

structs.name: Hash
structs.comment: A Lua table (ltable.c): open-addressed slots, rehashed at 70% use.
fields: GCnode: the next table of roottable

structs.name: LocVar
structs.comment: A local variable of a function's debug information: its name (NULL: a block end) and the line from which it is in scope; line -1 ends the list.

structs.name: TProtoFunc
structs.comment: A Lua function prototype (lfunc.c luaF_newproto). Grim's order: the constants first.

structs.name: Closure
structs.comment: A function closure (lfunc.c luaF_newclosure): the function (aConsts[0]) and its nelems upvalues after it.
fields: nelems + 1 values: the function, then the upvalues
